title: RMSNorm
goal:
LLaMA normalizes the input of every sub-layer with RMSNorm (Section 2.2, citing Zhang and Sennrich, 2019):

$$y_i = \frac{x_i}{\sqrt{\frac{1}{d}\sum_{j=1}^{d} x_j^2 + \epsilon}}\, g_i$$

Write `rmsnorm(x, g, eps=1e-6)`. `x` has shape `(..., d)` and `g` has shape `(d,)`. Normalize over the last axis only, and don't subtract the mean. The paper writes no $\epsilon$ in the formula; implementations add it inside the square root so that a zero vector doesn't divide by zero.
hints: The mean square is `np.mean(x ** 2, axis=-1, keepdims=True)`. Use `keepdims=True` so the division broadcasts.
Add `eps` to the mean square, then take the square root: `np.sqrt(ms + eps)`. Adding it after the square root gives a different number when `eps` is large.
Compare with LayerNorm: LayerNorm subtracts the mean and divides by the standard deviation. RMSNorm divides by the root mean square and keeps the mean.
